goal: At the user's instruction, an AI gets the day's claude -p work done overnight while nobody answers, so that it doesn't use up the daytime usage window: it queues the tasks with a start time and starts the queue detached; overnight three run at once, each stopped by the usage limit resuming in its own session once the limit resets, and one stopped seven times given up and logged; in the morning it tells the user which finished and which were given up, and takes the results in from the main session; and the AI of another plugin that runs claude -p unattended calls the wait-and-resume part instead of writing its own.

deliverable.name: The developers know whom overnight serves, the AI that arranges the work at the user's instruction and the AI of another plugin that runs claude -p unattended, and what each is after
